name: Semantic Response Caching
question: Has someone already asked this, in other words?
summary: Store whole answers keyed by the meaning of the question. Each new question is embedded and compared with cached questions; if one is similar enough, in the same scope and not expired, its stored answer is returned and the model is never called. This differs from prompt caching, where the provider reuses a processed prompt prefix but the model still writes a fresh answer. The risks are false hits (a similar but different question gets the wrong answer), stale answers after the source changes, and personal answers leaking between users.
useCases: High-volume support bots where many users ask the same FAQ in different words
Answers that depend only on shared content, such as plans, policies and how-to steps
Traffic where a lookup is far cheaper and faster than an LLM call

items.detail: how close a question must be to reuse an answer; lower means more hits and more false hits
global, per tenant or per user; personalised answers are never shared
FAQ-like intents only; account-specific and live-data intents bypass the cache
how long an entry lives before it must be regenerated
purge or version entries when the source document changes
hit rate, false-hit rate from sampled reviews, and ₹ saved net of lookups

steps: Classify intents and send account-specific or live-data questions straight to the model
Pick a threshold from a labelled set of paraphrase and near-miss pairs, not by feel
Tag every entry with its scope and the version of the source it came from
Sample hits for review, track false-hit rate and ₹ saved, and purge on source changes
pitfalls: A loose threshold returns confident answers to different questions: “roaming in UAE” is not “roaming in USA”
A global cache holding account answers shows one customer’s data to another
A long TTL keeps serving old prices after the tariff changes
remember: Cache the shared answers, never the personal ones. Tune the threshold on near misses.
caption: Illustrative: Tarang Mobile, a fictional telecom operator, with 1,00,000 questions a day, a 0.90 threshold, a global FAQ cache and account intents excluded.

comparison.needs: Medium: vector store, intent filter, reviews

code.text: def answer(question: str, user: dict) -> str:
if classify_intent(question) in ACCOUNT:          # live, personal data
return llm_answer(question, user=user)        # straight to the model
reply = llm_answer(question, user=None)           # shared facts only

steps.title: Keep personal questions out
steps.text: 40,000 of Tarang Mobile's 1,00,000 daily questions are about a customer's own bill, balance or SIM. Their answers depend on live, personal data, so they go straight to the model and are never looked up or stored.

steps.title: Set the threshold on near misses
steps.text: RedisVL measures cosine distance, so distance_threshold 0.10 means similarity 0.90. “How do I turn on roaming?” and “activate roaming?” score 0.94 and rightly share an answer. “Roaming packs for UAE” and “Roaming packs for USA” can score 0.91 and must not. Choose the threshold from labelled paraphrase and near-miss pairs.

steps.title: Scope the cache
steps.text: Every entry is tagged scope=global and the lookup filters on that tag. Only shared answers are stored, and they are generated without the user's details, so one customer's answer can never be served to another.

steps.title: Store on a miss, with a TTL
steps.text: On a miss the model answers and the reply is stored with a 24-hour TTL. The next paraphrase within a day is a hit; after 24 hours the entry expires and is written again.

steps.title: Invalidate when the source changes
steps.text: Each entry carries the tariff version it was written under. When the tariff page changes mid-week the version bumps, old entries stop matching at once, and the next question gets a fresh answer. Relying on the 24-hour TTL alone would serve about 5,610 stale price answers.

steps.title: Measure hits, false hits and ₹
steps.text: Log every hit with its distance and sample hits for human review. At 0.90 the cache answers 45,600 questions a day, about 720 of them false hits. At ₹0.40 per LLM answer and ₹0.01 per lookup on the 60,000 FAQ questions, it saves ₹18,240 − ₹600 = ₹17,640 a day.

pros: Repeated questions skip the model entirely, so they cost a lookup instead of an LLM call
Cached answers return in milliseconds instead of seconds
Popular answers stay consistent across thousands of customers
Stacks with prompt caching and routing on the questions that still miss
cons: False hits give a confident answer to a different question
Stale answers linger after prices or policies change unless you purge
A badly scoped cache can show one customer another customer’s data
Needs an embedding model, a vector store and a review loop to tune
avoidWhen: Most questions are personal or depend on live data, such as balances and order status (cache the shared facts the model uses instead)
Answers must reflect data that changes minute to minute (use prompt caching and fresh generation)

practice.scenario: Tarang Mobile, a fictional telecom operator, gets 1,00,000 support questions a day. 60,000 are FAQ-like, such as “How do I activate international roaming?” asked in dozens of ways, in English and Hinglish. A semantic cache with a 0.90 similarity threshold answers 45,600 of them from stored answers, while questions about a customer's own bill, balance or SIM skip the cache entirely. When the tariffs change mid-week, entries tagged with the old tariff version stop matching at once.

industries.use: Plan, roaming and recharge FAQs reused across millions of customers; bills and balances always generated fresh
“How do I raise a UPI dispute?” cached globally; “why was my UPI payment declined?” never cached
Return and delivery policy answers cached per region, with a purge when the policy page changes

practice.analogy: A railway enquiry counter with a board of printed answers to common questions. The clerk points to the board when a question matches one on it, but never for “where is my ticket?”, and the board is reprinted the day the timetable changes.

library.name: RedisVL SemanticCache
library.what: A semantic cache on Redis: set a cosine distance threshold and a TTL, tag entries with filterable fields such as scope and source version, then check() before calling the model and store() after a miss.

practice.note: classify_intent, llm_answer and current_tariff_version are stubs for your own intent classifier, model call and content version. RedisVL moved SemanticCache to redisvl.extensions.cache.llm in recent releases; older versions import it from redisvl.extensions.llmcache. The threshold script uses sentence-transformers; use the same embedding model as your cache.

samples.code:
from redisvl.extensions.cache.llm import SemanticCache
from redisvl.query.filter import Tag

ACCOUNT_INTENTS = {"bill", "balance", "recharge_status", "sim_block"}

cache = SemanticCache(
    name="tarang_faq",
    redis_url="redis://localhost:6379",
    distance_threshold=0.10,            # cosine distance: similarity >= 0.90
    ttl=24 * 3600,                      # seconds
    filterable_fields=[{"name": "scope", "type": "tag"},
                       {"name": "tariff_v", "type": "tag"}],
)


def answer(question: str, user: dict) -> str:
    if classify_intent(question) in ACCOUNT_INTENTS:
        return llm_answer(question, user=user)          # personal: never cached
    version = current_tariff_version()
    only = (Tag("scope") == "global") & (Tag("tariff_v") == version)
    hits = cache.check(prompt=question, filter_expression=only, num_results=1)
    if hits:
        return hits[0]["response"]
    reply = llm_answer(question, user=None)             # shared facts only
    cache.store(prompt=question, response=reply,
                filters={"scope": "global", "tariff_v": version})
    return reply

from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer

# Labelled pairs: True = same answer is correct, False = near miss
PAIRS = [
    ("How do I activate international roaming?", "activate roaming kaise kare", True),
    ("How do I turn on roaming?", "Enable roaming on my number", True),
    ("Roaming packs for UAE", "Roaming packs for USA", False),
    ("Price of the 299 plan", "Price of the 399 plan", False),
    ("How do I port my number to Tarang?", "Steps to port in to Tarang Mobile", True),
]

model = SentenceTransformer("all-MiniLM-L6-v2")


def similarity(a: str, b: str) -> float:
    ea, eb = model.encode([a, b], normalize_embeddings=True)
    return float(ea @ eb)


scored = [(similarity(a, b), same) for a, b, same in PAIRS]
for th in (0.80, 0.85, 0.90, 0.95, 0.98):
    hits = [same for sim, same in scored if sim >= th]
    false_hits = sum(1 for same in hits if not same)
    recall = sum(hits) / sum(same for _, same in scored)
    print(f"threshold {th:.2f}: recall {recall:.0%}, false hits {false_hits}")

numericDrill.question: Tarang Mobile sends its 60,000 daily FAQ questions through a semantic cache; account questions skip it. 45,600 are hits. An LLM answer costs ₹0.40 and each lookup ₹0.01. How many rupees a day does the cache save?
numericDrill.answer: Hits avoid 45,600 × ₹0.40 = ₹18,240 of LLM calls. Every FAQ question pays a lookup: 60,000 × ₹0.01 = ₹600. Net saving: ₹18,240 − ₹600 = ₹17,640 a day.

interview.question: How is a semantic response cache different from prompt caching?
interview.answer: Prompt caching is a provider feature: the processed prompt prefix is reused, but the model still generates a fresh answer, so answers stay correct and only input cost falls. A semantic cache sits in your own stack and returns a stored answer when a new question is similar enough, so the model is not called at all. It saves more per hit but can return a wrong answer on a near miss, a stale answer after the source changes, or another user's answer if scoped badly.

interview.question: How would you choose the similarity threshold?
interview.answer: Build a labelled set from real traffic: paraphrase pairs that should share an answer and near misses that should not, such as two plans or two countries. Embed them with the cache's own model, and for each threshold measure recall and the false-hit rate. Pick the loosest threshold whose false-hit rate is acceptable, then keep sampling live hits for review, because traffic drifts.

mistakes.mistake: Caching every intent in one global cache
mistakes.fix: Exclude account-specific and live-data intents, and tag entries with a scope

mistakes.mistake: Relying on TTL alone when source content changes
mistakes.fix: Tag entries with the source version and purge or stop matching when it changes

quiz.question: A telecom support bot gets 1,00,000 questions a day, and thousands of them ask how to activate roaming in different words. Each pays for a fresh LLM answer. Which technique targets this directly?
options: Prompt caching of the system prompt
A semantic response cache keyed by question embeddings
Batch processing overnight
A larger context window
quiz.explanation: Paraphrased repeats of the same FAQ can be served a stored answer when their embeddings are close enough, skipping the model entirely.

quiz.question: What is the key difference between prompt caching and a semantic response cache?
options: Prompt caching skips the model; a semantic cache does not
A semantic cache returns a stored answer without calling the model; prompt caching reuses the prefix but still generates a fresh answer
They are the same feature under different names
Prompt caching only works for images
quiz.explanation: Prompt caching cuts input cost while the model still answers; a semantic cache replaces the model call with a lookup.

quiz.question: A payments app caches answers globally. “Why was my UPI payment declined?” from one user returns another user’s answer. What is the root cause?
options: The threshold is too strict
An account-specific intent was cached in a global scope
The TTL is too short
The embedding model is too small
quiz.explanation: Personal questions look alike across users but their answers differ. They must skip the cache or be scoped per user.

quiz.question: A cache hits 45,600 of the 60,000 FAQ questions it checks each day. An LLM answer costs ₹0.40 and a lookup ₹0.01. What is the net daily saving?
“Visa rules for UAE” and “Visa rules for USA” have similarity 0.91. The threshold is 0.90. What happens?
options: A correct hit
A false hit: the UAE answer is served for the USA question
A miss
The cache asks the user to clarify
quiz.explanation: Near misses score high because most words match. Tune the threshold on labelled near-miss pairs, or add a check on key entities.

quiz.question: RedisVL’s SemanticCache is configured with distance_threshold=0.08. What similarity does that require?
options: At least 0.08
At least 0.92
At most 0.92
Exactly 0.08
quiz.explanation: Cosine distance is 1 minus similarity, so a distance of at most 0.08 means similarity of at least 0.92.

quiz.question: Which questions are good candidates for a global semantic cache? Select all that apply.
options: How do I download my policy document?
What does a cashless claim mean?
What is the status of my claim?
Which documents are needed to file a motor claim?
quiz.explanation: How-to and policy explanations are shared. Claim status depends on the customer’s live record and must be generated fresh.

quiz.question: Tariffs change on Wednesday. Cached price answers have a 7-day TTL and are not purged. Tariff hits run at 13,500 a day. Using the rule of thumb that stale answers ≈ daily hits × TTL in days ÷ 2, roughly how many stale answers go out?
quiz.explanation: Entries written before the change expire gradually over 7 days, so on average half are stale: 13,500 × 7 ÷ 2 = 47,250.

quiz.question: With the same 13,500 tariff hits a day, the TTL is cut to 24 hours, still without a purge. How many stale answers now?
quiz.explanation: 13,500 × 1 ÷ 2 = 6,750. A shorter TTL shrinks the stale window but does not close it; only a purge on change does.

quiz.question: A hospital chatbot caches “What are OPD timings?” globally. The timings change for the monsoon. What is the best fix?
options: Lower the threshold
Tag entries with the version of the timings page and purge or stop matching them when it changes
Switch to per-user scope
Increase the TTL
quiz.explanation: Invalidation tied to the source version retires old answers the moment the page changes, instead of waiting for expiry.

quiz.question: Which metrics should a team track for a semantic cache? Select all that apply.
options: Hit rate
False-hit rate from sampled human reviews
₹ saved net of lookup cost
Number of tokens in the system prompt
quiz.explanation: Hit rate and savings show value; the false-hit rate shows the price paid in wrong answers. Prompt length belongs to prompt caching.

quiz.question: A B2B help desk serves many companies with different contracts. Which scope fits cached answers about “our SLA for P1 tickets”?
options: Global
Per tenant
Per user
No cache at all is the only option
quiz.explanation: The answer depends on the company’s contract, not the individual user, so per-tenant scope shares it safely within one customer.

quiz.question: A per-user cache at 0.90 hits only 6% of questions. Why so low?
options: The threshold is too loose
Individual users rarely repeat their own questions, so there is little to reuse
Per-user caches are not allowed to store answers
Embeddings do not work per user
quiz.explanation: Reuse comes from many people asking the same shared question. A per-user cache sees few repeats.

quiz.question: Lowering the threshold from 0.90 to 0.80 raises the hit rate from 46% to 60% on FAQ traffic, and the daily saving rises too. What should you check before shipping?
options: Nothing: more saving is better
The false-hit rate on sampled hits, because many of the extra hits may be wrong answers
The embedding dimension
Whether the cache uses Redis
quiz.explanation: Saving counts false hits as money saved. Judge a threshold by false hits and saving together.

quiz.question: A wallet’s support bot adds a semantic cache. Which intents should skip it? Select all that apply.
options: Where is my refund?
What is my wallet balance?
How do I set a UPI PIN?
Why was my KYC rejected?
quiz.explanation: Refund status, balance and KYC outcome depend on the customer’s own records. Setting a UPI PIN is a shared how-to.

quiz.question: A cache stores answers generated with the student’s name and course inside them, then serves them globally. What is wrong?
options: Nothing, if the threshold is high
Personal details inside cached answers can be shown to other students
The TTL is too short
Embeddings cannot handle names
quiz.explanation: Only answers generated from shared facts, without personal details, belong in a shared scope.

quiz.question: 1,00,000 questions a day. The cache is checked only for the 60,000 FAQ questions, with 48,000 hits. What is the hit rate over all traffic?
quiz.explanation: 48,000 ÷ 1,00,000 = 48%. Against FAQ traffic alone it would be 80%, so say which base you use.

quiz.question: A team sets the threshold by trying a few questions by hand until results “look right”. What is the better approach?
options: Use the library default
Measure recall and false hits on a labelled set of paraphrase and near-miss pairs at several thresholds
Always use 0.99
Ask the LLM to pick a threshold
quiz.explanation: A labelled set turns the trade-off into numbers you can defend and re-check when traffic or the embedding model changes.

quiz.question: An NBFC’s FAQ cache must follow India’s DPDP Act principles. Which design choices help? Select all that apply.
options: Store only answers generated without personal data
Exclude loan-account intents from the cache
Set a TTL so entries do not live forever
Log full customer questions with PAN numbers in the cache key
quiz.explanation: Keeping personal data out of cached entries and limiting retention support data-minimisation. Storing PAN numbers in keys does the opposite. This is educational, not legal advice.

quiz.question: An LLM answer costs ₹0.50 and a lookup ₹0.02. At what hit rate on checked questions does the cache break even?
quiz.explanation: Every checked question pays ₹0.02; each hit saves ₹0.50. Break-even when hit rate × 0.50 = 0.02, so 4%.
